paper_metadata.title: Empirical Analysis of Classical and Quantum Algorithms for Portfolio Optimization: Enhancing Financial Decision-Making through Quantum Computing

summary: The paper compares QAOA, Sampling VQE, and an exact eigensolver with classical portfolio methods on 20 NSE stocks (2021–2024). Reported prediction errors show QAOA achieving MSE 0.005, VQE 0.007, and the exact eigensolver 0.006, compared with GA at 0.0105 and much larger errors for MVO (0.946) and SA (0.65). However, no quantum hardware, circuit sizes, or runtime benchmarks are reported.

experiments.description: Portfolio optimization experiment comparing QAOA against VQE, Exact Minimum Eigen Solver, and classical baselines on 20 NSE stocks using historical return data.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Portfolio selection formulated from expected returns and covariance matrix; discrete portfolio allocation optimized with QAOA. The paper does not specify the exact qubit-to-variable mapping.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Maximize f(x) = μ^T x − q · x^T Σ x
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Budget constraint with portfolio budget set to half the number of assets; no explicit penalty formulation reported for QAOA.

problem_instance.description: Portfolio optimization over 20 equities from the National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) using historical adjusted closing prices from 2021-01-01 to 2024-01-01.

preprocessing: daily returns computed as percentage changes in adjusted closing prices

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Adjusted closing prices were downloaded with yfinance; missing values were excluded; daily returns were computed; return data was normalized and standardized.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Performance compared using MSE, RMSE, and MAE against an equal-weight portfolio benchmark; results reported for a single experimental setup.

implementation_details.classical_solver: Classical optimizers/baselines include MVO, GA, and SA; QAOA implementation details such as optimizer and framework are not reported.
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Historical price preprocessing, missing-value removal, return calculation, normalization, standardization, covariance matrix estimation, predicted returns estimation.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Portfolio weights and return/error metrics compared across methods.

speedup_claims.caveats: The paper reports empirical accuracy improvements for QAOA over classical baselines, but no asymptotic or wall-clock speedup is quantified.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Not specified; qubit counts, circuit depth, shots, and hardware backend are not reported.
limiting_factors: No real quantum hardware used or reported
No circuit size, qubit count, or runtime data
Comparison focuses only on prediction error metrics rather than computational advantage
Classical baselines not rigorously tuned or benchmarked

notes: The paper explicitly reports QAOA as one of the evaluated quantum algorithms and provides the portfolio objective function and dataset details, but does not specify the QAOA circuit size, depth, optimizer, backend, or qubit count.
num_qubits and circuit_depth are not reported; no device or circuit diagram details are given, so they cannot be reliably inferred.
speedup_order is not characterized asymptotically; the paper reports empirical metric improvements only.

Authors claim quantum algorithms outperform classical methods based on lower MSE values (QAOA 0.005 vs GA 0.0105), but experiments appear to be classical simulations with no hardware or runtime comparison.
Problem size (20 assets) is far below scales where combinatorial optimization advantage could emerge.
